Formulation:
Predisposing factors: Athletic lifestyle with high training demands; limited recorded coping strategies for anxiety/insomnia.  
Precipitating factors: Recent increase in running mileage leading to knee pain, triggering anxiety about injury and loss of marathon goal.  
Perpetuating factors: Ongoing worry, continued exercise despite pain, irregular sleep hygiene, PRN benzodiazepine use.  
Protective factors: Good insight, proactive help-seeking, physically active, no substance dependence, supportive doctor-patient relationship.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Health-related anxiety about knee injury
- Patient Goal(s): Understand knee condition; reduce worry; maintain training safely
- Clinical Goal(s): Decrease anxiety symptoms; improve coping strategies; monitor for escalation
- Actions (Patient):
  • Practice recommended coping strategies (e.g., relaxation, paced breathing)  
  • Follow physiotherapy referral and adhere to modified training plan  
  • Monitor anxiety levels and sleep patterns; seek review if worsening
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide brief psychoeducation on common overuse knee injuries and prognosis  
  • Reinforce graded return-to-run plan with physiotherapist  
  • Offer information on anxiety-management resources (e.g., online CBT modules)  
  • Review anxiety and sleep in 4–6 weeks or sooner if symptoms escalate

Secondary Problem: Intermittent insomnia
- Patient Goal(s): Achieve consistent, restful sleep without reliance on Xanax
- Clinical Goal(s): Improve sleep hygiene; minimize benzodiazepine use
- Actions (Patient):
  • Implement consistent bedtime routine; limit screens/caffeine before bed  
  • Use melatonin as first-line; reserve Xanax only if directed  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide sleep-hygiene hand-out; discuss risks of regular benzodiazepine use  
  • Reassess sleep and consider non-pharmacologic options (CBT-I) at follow-up

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Knee injury prognosis; use of ice/rest; anxiety-management techniques; sleep hygiene; safe medication use
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Persistent worry interfering with daily function; increasing benzodiazepine use; marked decline in sleep
- Coping Strategies: Relaxation exercises, graded activity plan, seeking support from physiotherapist/GP if anxiety worsens

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (verbal during consultation)
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: To be emailed
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently; physiotherapist involved for knee management
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: 4–6 weeks or sooner if symptoms escalate
